milwaukee-speech.collection: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
milwaukee-speech.crop: re-cropped from the LOC master TIFF (4310x5803), x 4-93%, y 4.5-88%; the black glass-negative rim on all four sides and the Bain agency's painted caption "ELBERT MARTIN & BULLET-PIERCED SPEECH" are outside the crop
milwaukee-speech.note: Bain glass negative. The painted caption reads correctly while the scratched negative number reads mirror-reversed — the Bain lettering was applied to the glass side, so on this plate the two disagree. There is no legible text inside the frame, so whether the image itself is laterally reversed cannot be settled from the plate, and it has been left as the Library holds it. Compare california-delegates, where in-frame street signage does settle it.

california-delegates.description: [California delegates cheering on stagecoach at the 1912 Republican National Convention held at the Chicago Coliseum, Chicago, Illinois, June 18-22, 1912]
california-delegates.rights: No known restrictions on publication. For more information, see George Grantham Bain Collection - Rights and Restrictions Information https://www.loc.gov/rr/print/res/274_bain.html
california-delegates.collection: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
california-delegates.crop: re-cropped from the LOC master TIFF (5723x4203), x 3-88%, y 2.5-95.5%, then FLIPPED HORIZONTALLY; the black glass-negative rim and the Bain agency's painted caption "CAL. DEL. CHEER..." are outside the crop
california-delegates.note: The Library's scan of this Bain glass negative is laterally reversed. The proof is inside the frame: the street sign for the Ford & Johnson Building, a real Chicago furniture house, reads backwards in the LOC file and reads correctly once flipped. The Bain agency's painted captions read the right way round in the unflipped scan because they were applied to the glass side of the plate, not the emulsion — which is why they now read backwards and have been cropped away. The pencilled negative number at the top right is on the glass side too and still reads reversed.
